label: g1152-ewr-tick-perf
_why: THE TICK COST OF THE RULED RESEARCH-WEIGHT RULE (BALANCE_FRAMEWORK 10.119 item 3, ruled 2026-11-21: -20% at the literacy line, -50% while the entry is TICKING, read by the cheap form), a PERFORMANCE probe; the user's go-ahead 2026-11-21: "Go on with the probe with the four 10-year runs, alternating." The ticking signal adds a monthly pulse to every one of the 339 stage entries (226 new, 113 extended): when an open stage's bar has risen since the value it stored on itself last month, an expiring country flag pmr_adv_<tech> is set, which the AI weight reads. Probe 5 (F279) found the first form (a stage open with progress) invisible against the canon; this measures the ruled form the same way. Never economy data.

_arms.ewr2: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.g1151-canon-bz-dcu-ra-il-aw-ewr2.json} - the canon + research_events.entry_weight_rule { lowered 0.8, advancing 0.5, signal tick } (sha256 c6f20491d4509461; field diff: that key and its record)

_comparison: seconds of play per in-game year from each run's run.log tick lines, per attempt, ewr2 against the canon runs played beside them (probe 5's reading, F279: the wall-clock reader drops probes). Beside it, a behaviour check on the ewr2 runs' kept 1846 saves: journal entries carry pmr_bp, and some countries carry pmr_adv_<tech> flags.

_predictions.cost: inside the noise again (a few percent between two runs of one arm): about 2,300 open entries late in the game and fewer early, each doing two or three variable operations a month; an upper bound of about +1% if each pulse costs as much as the bar's own evaluation (F220: the entries' monthly price)
_predictions.signal: the saves show pmr_bp on open stage entries and pmr_adv_<tech> on countries whose entries ticked in the last 45 days; error.log shows no class from the new pulses
_predictions.game: four runs of about 12 minutes, with builds about 60 minutes

_stop_rule: none: every run plays to its date.
_caveats: Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (landmine L30).
A performance probe (probe: performance): the readers drop it; quote nothing about the economy from it (10.118).
